name: worldquant_iqc
description: WorldQuant International Quant Championship. Alpha expressions evaluated on WQ BRAIN across regions / universes.

cross_sectional: neutralize(x, group) — subtract group mean (e.g. industry, sector)
power(x, n), signed_power(x, n) — non-linear transforms
time_series: ts_mean(x, d) — rolling mean over d days
ts_arg_max(x, d), ts_arg_min(x, d) — bar offset of extreme in window
ts_corr(x, y, d), ts_covariance(x, y, d) — rolling pairwise
ts_decay_linear(x, d) — linearly weighted average (most recent heavier)
risk_transforms: divide by ts_std_dev(returns, d) to target volatility
neutralize by ts_mean across universe to remove market beta
group_neutralize by Industry or SubIndustry to remove sector beta
common_fields: close, open, high, low, volume, vwap
fundamental N (fnd) — a wide range of accounting items; e.g. fnd13 is book value

code_skeleton:
# WQ BRAIN alpha expression. Paste into the BRAIN IDE.
# Target: cross-sectional, vol-targeted, sector-neutralized.

# Example: short-term reversal on liquid names
returns_5d = ts_mean(returns, 5)
alpha = -rank(returns_5d)
alpha = group_neutralize(alpha, subindustry)
alpha = scale(alpha)

# Alternate: momentum-with-low-vol bias
# mom = ts_mean(returns, 63) - ts_mean(returns, 5)   # 3mo - 1wk
# stability = 1 / (ts_std_dev(returns, 20) + 0.0001)
# alpha = rank(mom) * rank(stability)
# alpha = group_neutralize(alpha, industry)
anti_patterns: Using look-ahead operators (accessing future prices, future fundamentals, future reports).
Dividing by a value that can be zero without a constant — produces NaN/Inf that BRAIN rejects.
Over-fit IS Sharpe that collapses OOS: IQC rewards universality, not a single period.
Ignoring neutralization: raw-scale signals without sector/market neutralization are usually rejected on the universality check.
Turnover below 3% or above 60% gets flagged inactive / excessive.
Max weight per stock breach — scale/rank and cap with the appropriate operator.
Signals that rely on a single fundamental that is sparse across universe.
submission_requirements: Alpha expression in the BRAIN DSL (operators + fields above).
Positive OOS Sharpe, positive OOS IR.
Passes universality, weight, and turnover checks.
Neutralized by SubIndustry (or Industry) unless the signal is market-breadth.
Typically one-line or few-line expression — excess complexity is penalized.
past_round_notes: Rank-of-rolling-mean beats raw rolling mean 9 times out of 10 because cross-sectional rank is universality-friendly.
Volatility-scaled signals (alpha / ts_std_dev(returns, 20)) produce steadier Sharpes across regimes.
Combining two weakly-correlated alphas via rank-averaging usually beats either alone.
Industry neutralization is almost always additive; market-cap neutralization helps when signal is cap-biased.
Short-term reversal (negative rank of 5-day return) is the classic starter — still works in most regions.
prompt_addendum: Context: WorldQuant IQC on the BRAIN platform. Output ONLY a BRAIN DSL alpha expression — NOT a Python script. Follow the Alpha-GPT three-stage structure: (1) Polisher: clarify the trading idea and identify relevant data fields; (2) Developer: write a valid BRAIN DSL expression using operators from the operator reference; (3) Analyst: check for divide-by-zero, missing neutralization, and scale. ALWAYS apply the canonical pipeline: winsorize → ts_zscore/ts_rank → rank/zscore → group_neutralize(x, subindustry) → scale(x). Optimize for OOS Sharpe > 1.25 and universality across regions. Keep the expression concise — BRAIN penalizes complexity. DO NOT print STRATENGINE_STATS. DO NOT output Python imports or class definitions.
